title: Range Weak Exit Note
summary: Research note about weak exits in range regimes.

insights.summary: Weak exits should be tightened during low-volatility ranges.
insights.rationale: Losses deepen when entries stay open during squeeze breakdowns.
insights.suggestedMutation: Tighten exits during range_squeeze when momentum weakens after entry.

title: Regime-aware exit tightening and trade-count recovery for 120m QQQ strategy
summary: External retrieval failed, so the strongest actionable synthesis is to avoid broader hard regime blocks and instead use narrowly scoped regime-conditional exit tightening, asymmetric counter-trend throttling in trend_down, and trade-count recovery via selective re-entry or setup-tier gating. For 120m QQQ longs, prioritize reducing adverse excursion in range_squeeze and weak counter-trend holds in trend_down without globally cutting participation.
problemTags: How to design regime-specific loser exits for low-trend/range-squeeze conditions that reduce adverse excursion without overcutting acceptable trades on 120m equity index systems.
Methods for blocking or tapering counter-trend long exposure during trend_down regimes while preserving enough trade count to pass tradability constraints.
Practical approaches for adding time-in-trade, momentum-fade, or staged partial exits that improve drawdown control more than they reduce expectancy.
Techniques for recovering low trade count after tightening exits/filters, especially via selective re-entry, asymmetric gating by setup tier, or narrower application of regime blocks.

insights.summary: Use regime-specific loser exits only in low-trend states rather than tightening exits globally.
insights.rationale: The current search context suggests the local edge problem is concentrated in range/range_squeeze, where trades are more likely to stall or mean-revert before reaching normal swing objectives. Global stop tightening usually lowers expectancy and trade survivability in better trend states, so restricting tighter management to low-trend regimes is the cleaner mutation.
insights.suggestedMutation: In Pine, when regime == range or range_squeeze, replace the base stop with min(baseStop, entryPrice - k1*ATR) and add a close-condition exit if barsSinceEntry >= n1 and maxRunupATR < r1. Leave trend_up exits unchanged.

insights.summary: Prefer tapered counter-trend suppression in trend_down over full long-entry bans.
insights.rationale: A hard block on longs during trend_down may help drawdown but commonly causes low trade count and fails tradability constraints. A softer rule preserves participation by allowing only higher-quality long setups, such as stronger momentum confirmation, shallower pullback entries, or reduced position sizing in downtrend regimes.
insights.suggestedMutation: In Pine, if regime == trend_down, require setupScore >= highTierThreshold for entry, or require close > fastEMA and ROC(len) > 0 before allowing longs; optionally reduce qty by 50% instead of blocking all entries.

insights.summary: Add momentum-fade and time-in-trade exits as secondary exits for non-progressing positions.
insights.rationale: On 120m index systems, many problematic trades are not immediate stop-outs but slow non-performers that tie up exposure and later degrade into larger losers. A staged exit triggered by lack of progress or loss of short-term momentum can cut these positions earlier while avoiding unnecessary exits on trades that quickly establish favorable excursion.
insights.suggestedMutation: Track barsInTrade, highestSinceEntry, and runupATR = (highestSinceEntry - entryPrice)/ATR. If barsInTrade >= n2 and runupATR < r2, exit. Separately, if regime in [range, range_squeeze, trend_down] and RSI falls below x after entry or close crosses below fastEMA after failing to exceed r3*ATR runup, exit or trim 50%.

insights.summary: Recover lost trade count with selective re-entry after tightened exits instead of loosening all filters.
insights.rationale: When stricter exits improve drawdown but reduce completed winners, selective re-entry is often less damaging than removing the protective rule. Re-entry is especially useful after a time-stop or momentum-fade exit where the original thesis may reassert shortly after a shallow shakeout.
insights.suggestedMutation: After an exit caused by time-stop or momentum-fade, allow one re-entry within m bars if price reclaims fastEMA or breaks the prior swing high and regime is not trend_down hard-risk state. Use a stricter trigger than the initial entry and cap to one re-entry per signal cluster.

insights.summary: Apply protective logic by setup tier so weaker setups get tighter exits and stronger setups retain baseline freedom.
insights.rationale: If all entries are managed identically, exit tightening often harms the subset of trades that actually drive expectancy. Segmenting entries by internal quality score lets the strategy cut weak-context trades faster while preserving room for higher-conviction setups, which is useful when AF is trapped between drawdown reduction and tradability.
insights.suggestedMutation: Define setup tiers from existing features (trend alignment, momentum, pullback depth, breadth/vol filter). For low-tier entries, enable tighter ATR stop and shorter time-stop in range_squeeze or trend_down; for high-tier entries, keep original stop and disable early momentum-fade unless loss exceeds y*ATR.

title: Low-complexity regime-aware mutation patterns for drawdown control and trade-count preservation
summary: No new empirical paper signal was produced because retrieval/generation failed, but the batch clearly points to a practical need: use compact single-block Pine mutations that localize regime awareness to one entry or exit clause at a time. For QQQ 120m-style systems, the safest path is asymmetric counter-trend control first via light confirmation or size taper in trend_down, then localized range/range_squeeze loser exits or time stops, and finally selective trade-count recovery through narrow re-entry logic rather than broad entry expansion.
problemTags: Implementation-safe single-block Pine mutation patterns that reduce generation failures when adding localized regime-aware logic.
Minimal-complexity trend_down long-taper or confirmation rules that preserve trade count better than full regime blocks.
Localized loser-exit and time-stop patterns for range/range_squeeze that are simple enough to express without multi-subsystem rewrites.
Low-trade-count recovery methods after exit tightening that rely on selective re-entry or narrower regime application with minimal code footprint.
Conflict-resolution guidance for sequencing repairs when objectives alternate between entry-gating recovery and exit-tightening drawdown control.

insights.summary: Prefer a single appended confirmation clause for long entries only during trend_down instead of adding a full regime subsystem.
insights.rationale: The brief emphasizes generation-safe localized logic and preserving trade count. A narrow asymmetric rule such as requiring one extra bullish condition only when a simple downtrend proxy is true reduces counter-trend exposure without suppressing all trades in neutral/up regimes.
insights.suggestedMutation: Define `trendDown = close < ta.ema(close, 50) and ta.ema(close, 20) < ta.ema(close, 50)`. Replace `longCondition` with `longCondition := longCondition and (not trendDown or close > high[1])` or `and (not trendDown or ta.rsi(close, 14) > 52)`. Keep all other logic unchanged.

insights.summary: When full blocking damages tradability, taper position size in trend_down rather than rejecting entries outright.
insights.rationale: The problem statement specifically asks for methods that preserve trade count better than full regime blocks. Size taper keeps signal participation while reducing damage from weak counter-trend longs, which is often easier to insert in one block than restructuring the signal stack.
insights.suggestedMutation: Compute `riskMult = trendDown ? 0.5 : 1.0` and apply it directly to order quantity, e.g. `strategy.entry('L', strategy.long, qty=baseQty * riskMult)` or if percent sizing is used, `qty_percent = basePct * riskMult`. Do not change entry trigger logic.

insights.summary: Use a regime-localized loser exit in range or squeeze conditions instead of globally tightening exits.
insights.rationale: The brief asks for simple loser-exit and time-stop patterns under range/range_squeeze. A localized exit only when the trade is losing and the market is compressed/rangy can cut adverse excursion without harming trend trades, which helps preserve frequency better than universal stop tightening.
insights.suggestedMutation: Define `rangeRegime = math.abs(ta.ema(close, 20) - ta.ema(close, 50)) < ta.atr(14) * 0.3` or `bbWidth = (ta.bb(close,20,2)[1] - ta.bb(close,20,2)[2]) / close; rangeRegime = bbWidth < bbThresh`. Then add `if strategy.position_size > 0 and rangeRegime and close < strategy.position_avg_price and barsSinceEntry >= 2 strategy.close('L')`.

insights.summary: Apply a short time stop only to stalled losing positions in non-trending regimes, not to all trades.
insights.rationale: Time stops can control drawdown, but global time exits often cut winners and reduce expectancy. Restricting the stop to losing trades in range-like conditions keeps the code small and limits damage to the part of the distribution most associated with churn.
insights.suggestedMutation: Track `barsInTrade = ta.barssince(strategy.position_size == 0)`. Add `if strategy.position_size > 0 and rangeRegime and barsInTrade >= 3 and close <= strategy.position_avg_price * 1.002 strategy.close('L')`. Thresholds can be tightened or loosened in one line.

insights.summary: After adding tighter exits, recover trade count with selective same-signal re-entry windows instead of broadening the whole entry filter.
insights.rationale: The batch notes that exit tightening can collapse tradability and asks for low-footprint recovery methods. A narrow re-entry rule after a localized stop-out can restore participation where the original thesis quickly reasserts, while avoiding blanket loosening that reintroduces poor-quality entries.
insights.suggestedMutation: Store a flag on exit such as `stoppedRangeLoser := rangeRegime and close < strategy.position_avg_price`. For the next 1-3 bars, allow re-entry only if original `longCondition` is true and price reclaims a fast filter, e.g. `reentryOk = stoppedRangeLoser[1] or stoppedRangeLoser[2]` and `longCondition := longCondition or (reentryOk and close > ta.ema(close, 20))`.

title: Implementation-safe localized Pine mutation patterns for exit repair, drawdown control, and trade-count recovery
summary: Primary gap is not new QQQ 120m trading logic but mutation robustness: use single-locus, single-block Pine edits that narrow exits by regime, avoid new persistent state, and preserve trade count via selective scope reduction or immediate replacement rather than repeated broad exit-tightening directives. When generation fails repeatedly, pivot from richer exit logic to simpler localized edits at entry timing, slot allocation, or replacement level.
problemTags: Implementation-safe single-block Pine Script mutation templates for localized exit or risk edits that minimize generation failure under strict 'one behavioral change' constraints.
Research on robust prompt/program-repair patterns for agentic code mutation when repeated natural-language repair directives cause generation collapse or contradictory instructions.
Minimal regime-localized exit patterns for range/range_squeeze and trend-down conditions that can be expressed in one line/block without adding new state yet still preserve trade count.
Low-complexity recovery tactics after tighter exits, especially selective re-entry or narrower regime application that can be encoded with minimal code footprint.

Actionable sequencing rules for when to stop repeating exit-tightening directives and pivot to implementation simplification or alternate loci such as entry timing taper, slot management, or replacement logic.

insights.summary: Prefer one-condition exit narrowing inside an existing exit block, gated by an already-available regime flag such as range/range_squeeze or trend-down.
insights.rationale: The observed failures came from overconstrained repair instructions, not lack of exit ideas. A minimal mutation that only changes one boolean branch has lower syntax and coordination risk than adding new vars, subsystems, or multi-branch logic. For QQQ 120m, regime-localized tightening is safer than globally tighter exits because it cuts drawdown where mean reversion/trend failure is more likely without collapsing trade count across all regimes.
insights.suggestedMutation: Inside the current long exit condition, append a localized clause using existing series only, e.g. `longExit := longExit or (isRange and close < ta.ema(close, 10))` or `longExit := longExit or (trendDown and close < low[1])`; do not create new state, functions, or additional orders.

insights.summary: If regime exits are hard to express safely, use a stateless bar-count time stop derived from existing position metadata instead of adding tracking variables.
insights.rationale: A time stop is implementation-safe when expressed through built-in trade metadata or existing bar counters because it avoids cross-block dependencies. On 120m QQQ, many drawdown episodes come from overstaying stale longs after momentum decay; a bounded holding period can repair weak exits while remaining localized. Using built-ins lowers generation failure compared with custom state machines.
insights.suggestedMutation: Add one extra exit clause using built-ins only, e.g. `longExit := longExit or (strategy.position_size > 0 and bar_index - strategy.opentrades.entry_bar_index(strategy.opentrades - 1) >= 8)` guarded with `strategy.opentrades > 0` if needed; keep it in the same existing exit block.

insights.summary: After tighter exits reduce trade count too much, recover by narrowing the new exit to only the worst regime rather than loosening all exits.
insights.rationale: Low-complexity recovery is best achieved by reducing the scope of the new behavior, not by layering re-entry/stateful exceptions that increase code fragility. In QQQ 120m systems, over-tight exits often hurt trending segments more than choppy ones; restricting the mutation to range_squeeze or trend-down regimes preserves most original participation while still addressing the main drawdown pocket.
insights.suggestedMutation: Wrap the added exit clause with the narrowest existing regime predicate, e.g. change `longExit := longExit or close < ta.ema(close, 10)` to `longExit := longExit or (isRangeSqueeze and close < ta.ema(close, 10))`; if already regime-gated, remove secondary gates and keep only the highest-value regime filter.

insights.summary: When repeated exit-tightening attempts fail or conflict, pivot to a small entry-timing taper in weak regimes instead of adding more exit logic.
insights.rationale: The batch history suggests diminishing returns from repeated exit directives. A simpler and often safer behavioral shift is to slightly delay or filter entries in the same bad regime causing drawdown, which reduces adverse trades without creating downstream exit interactions. For QQQ 120m, avoiding late or counter-trend entries in range_squeeze/trend-down environments can improve drawdown while preserving cleaner trend trades.
insights.suggestedMutation: Modify only the existing long entry boolean with one extra conjunct using existing filters, e.g. `longEntry := longEntry and not isRangeSqueeze` or `longEntry := longEntry and close > ta.ema(close, 20)` in trend-down contexts; do not touch exits in the same mutation.

insights.summary: Use a strict repair sequence: one localized edit, then validate; after two generation failures on the same locus, simplify the instruction or switch loci to replacement/slot logic.
insights.rationale: Program-repair literature and the retrieval context both indicate repeated natural-language restatement can increase contradiction and failure. For strategy mutation, the safest path is monotonic simplification: specify exact edit locus, exact allowed change type, and ban new state. If that still fails twice, switch from exit repair to replacement logic such as immediate re-eligibility after exit or slot gating, which can recover trade count with smaller code impact than re-entry subsystems.
insights.suggestedMutation: Prompt/template rule for AF: `Edit exactly one existing block. Add one boolean clause only. No new vars/functions/orders.` If two failed generations occur, next mutation must target a different single block such as `longEntry` or slot gating, e.g. `canLong := canLong and not trendDown` or permit replacement only when `close > ema`.

title: Local pullback directive
summary: Prioritize locally testable QQQ 120m pullback-in-trend variants while TradingView remains secondary for calibration; emphasize earlier pullback entries over breakout/extension chasing, with bounded exits and explicit risk controls.

insights.summary: Bias research toward pullback entries inside an established uptrend rather than breakout confirmation entries.
insights.rationale: For QQQ 120m, breakout-style entries often arrive after substantial extension and can degrade reward-to-risk. A local-first workflow supports systematic testing of pullback triggers without dependence on TradingView editor availability.
insights.suggestedMutation: Require a bullish trend filter such as close > EMA(50) and EMA(20) > EMA(50), then enter long only when price pulls back 1-3 bars toward EMA(20) or lower Bollinger/Keltner mid-zone and closes back above prior bar high. Block entries if distance from EMA(20) exceeds a max extension threshold like 1.5-2.0 ATR.

insights.summary: Add an overextension gate before entry so pullbacks are bought only when the trend is still statistically normal, not exhausted.
insights.rationale: A common failure in trend-pullback systems is buying a shallow dip after an already stretched move. On 120m QQQ, this can lead to poor follow-through or immediate mean reversion.
insights.suggestedMutation: Add a pre-entry filter: reject longs when close is above EMA(20) by more than X ATR, when RSI(14) is above a threshold such as 68-72 before the pullback, or when 3-bar run-up exceeds a percent threshold. In Pine, compute extension = (close - ema20) / atr(14) and require extension < maxExt before signal re-arming.

insights.summary: Use a two-step pullback trigger to improve entry timing: trend qualification first, then local reversal confirmation.
insights.rationale: Entering on touch alone can catch falling pullbacks; entering on full breakout confirmation can be too late. A staged trigger balances earlier fills with reduced adverse selection.
insights.suggestedMutation: Stage 1: trend regime true for N bars. Stage 2: identify pullback low into EMA(10/20), VWAP proxy, or channel midline. Enter only after a reversal condition such as bullish engulfing, close above previous high, or stochastic/RSI turn-up from a non-oversold trend zone. Implement with a pullbackSetup boolean that arms for 1-3 bars and expires if not confirmed.

insights.summary: Keep exits bounded and adaptive to avoid turning pullback entries into large drawdowns during failed trend continuation.
insights.rationale: Pullback systems can enter earlier, which improves upside but also increases exposure to failed continuation. Strong risk framing is needed on 120m tech index behavior.
insights.suggestedMutation: Set initial stop below pullback swing low or 1.2-1.8 ATR, whichever is tighter. Add partial profit at 1R, then trail the remainder with EMA(20), chandelier ATR, or last swing low. Include a time stop such as exit after 4-8 bars if price fails to make a new trade high.
